issues.description: The problem text instructs students to use StringBuilder for the Animal name attribute, but the UML in the problem shows the name as String and the provided solution implements the name as a String field. This internal contradiction (problem text vs UML) and the mismatch with the solution will confuse students about which type to implement and may cause incompatibilities with reference code or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended type for Animal.name consistent across the problem statement, UML, template, and solution. Either: (A) change the problem text to remove the StringBuilder requirement and instruct students to use String (and update UML to String), or (B) update the solution and any template skeletons to use StringBuilder for the name field and adjust getters/setters and usages (and update the UML to reflect StringBuilder). Ensure all examples and tests expect the same type.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly instructs that the Animal.name attribute should use StringBuilder for efficient modifications, but the solution implementation (and template usage in Main) use a plain String for the name (constructor parameter, field, and accessors). This mismatch between the specified attribute type in the problem text and the implemented type in the code can confuse students about the expected representation and which type they should use when implementing getters/setters and constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation consistent: either update the solution and template to use a StringBuilder field for Animal.name (with corresponding getter/setter that expose/accept a StringBuilder or provide String-based convenience methods), or update the problem statement to require a String name. Prefer updating the code to use StringBuilder if the textual requirement is intentional; ensure constructor signatures and getName()/setName() reflect the chosen type.
